body.statement:
Within the fully Markovian class \(Mone\), the compatible causal set is exactly
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U].
\]
The Ejaz--Bareinboim \(\rho\)-Markovian class may be strictly larger because it permits within-instance latent confounding.  If \(F\) is nonconstant, nonidentification transfers to that larger class by subclass inclusion.  If their complete procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\), \([L,U]\) remains the sharp set for \(Mone\) but is not asserted to be sharp for the larger class.  If \(F\) is constant, then \(L=U\) identifies the query over \(Mone\); this point-identification conclusion transfers to the Ejaz--Bareinboim class only when the supplied graph excludes the additional confounding so that the two classes coincide.  The unsupported status of \(rstar\) alone does not imply \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).
body.justification: The theorem is the exactly certifiable univariate specialization and distinguishes subclass sharpness from conclusions that transfer to the larger rho-Markovian class.
body.gap: Ejaz and Bareinboim establish completeness on a larger class that may include latent confounding; the present interval is sharp for the fully Markovian subclass and is not presented as their class's sharp range.
body.consumer: Experiment 6.1 can accompany its fitted N3 point with the certified fully Markovian range and an explicit model-class qualification.
body.proof_tex:
Under \(\texttt{ass:one-unsupported-row}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:binary-free-row}\), the generalized unsupported-row objects
specialize to
\[
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}=\{rstar\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}
 =\{(1-q,q):0\leq q\leq 1\}.
\]
Comparing \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) with
\(\texttt{def:finite-unsupported-model-class}\), all the remaining
membership requirements are identical: the same finite schema and graph
are used, the same source and target groundings are induced, the ground
noises are mutually independent, mechanisms are type shared, the source
laws \(Psrc\) are reproduced, and the rows in \(K\) are used at all
positive-source-support keys.  Hence, in this specialization,
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}=Mone\).  The two query definitions then give
\(Q_{\mathrm{fin}}=Q\).  Finally, replaying
\(\texttt{def:multivariate-target-polynomial}\) with
\(p_{rstar}=(1-q,q)\) is exactly the replay defining \(F\); equivalently,
this is the equality proved in \(\texttt{lem:polynomial-reduction}\).
Thus
\[
 \Phi\bigl((1-q,q)\bigr)=F(q),\qquad 0\leq q\leq1.
\]
Applying \(\texttt{thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows}\) to this
specialization yields
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1]).
\]
In particular, the reverse inclusion is witnessed by compatible
finite-noise, type-shared models and is not merely an outer bound.

It remains to identify the endpoints appearing in the statement.  The
polynomial \(F\) is continuous.  Therefore it attains a minimum and a
maximum on the compact interval \([0,1]\), as also follows from the compact
attainment argument in
\(\texttt{thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows}\).  If \(F\) is nonconstant
and \(c\in(0,1)\) is either optimizer, then for every sufficiently small
\(h>0\) the two one-sided difference quotients at \(c\) have the
appropriate opposite weak signs.  Differentiability gives
\[
 F'(c)
 =\lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{F(c+h)-F(c)}{h}
 =\lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{F(c)-F(c-h)}{h}=0.
\]
Consequently every optimizer is either \(0\), \(1\), or a feasible
distinct real root of \(F'\), and hence belongs to \(Ccrit\) by
\(\texttt{def:critical-candidates}\).  Conversely \(Ccrit\subseteq[0,1]\).
It follows from the definitions of \(L\) and \(U\) that
\[
 \min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\min_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=L,
 \qquad
 \max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\max_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=U.
\]
If \(F\) is constant, all candidate and interval values coincide, so the
same two equalities hold.  The continuous image of an interval is
connected, while compactness makes it closed and bounded; therefore its
image is precisely the interval between its attained extrema:
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U].
\]

We next justify the comparator qualifications.  By
\(\texttt{lem:ejaz-bareinboim-rho-markovian-scope}\), the
Ejaz--Bareinboim \(\rho\)-Markovian class permits a ground instance to
have shared exogenous parents.  A model in \(Mone\) is the special case
with no such sharing, because
\(\texttt{ass:markovian-noises}\) makes the noises of distinct ground
endogenous variables mutually independent.  Its observed domains are
finite by \(\texttt{ass:finite-domains}\), and the fixed finite ground
graphs have a finite uniform bound on relational-parent multiset size.
Thus \(Mone\) is a subclass of that comparator class, and the inclusion
can be strict when additional within-instance latent confounding is
allowed.

If \(F\) is nonconstant, choose \(q_1,q_2\in[0,1]\) with
\(F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)\).  The already proved reverse inclusion supplies
\(M_1,M_2\in Mone\) such that
\[
 Q(M_1)=F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)=Q(M_2).
\]
Both models also belong to the larger comparator class.  Hence the query
is not point identified there either.  A report of
\(\mathsf{FAIL}\) by the comparator procedure does not alter the equality
\(\Theta=[L,U]\) for \(Mone\), but none of the preceding inclusions bounds
the values of the extra confounded models; sharpness for the larger class
is therefore not asserted.  If \(F\) is constant, the first part gives
\(L=U\) and point identification on \(Mone\).  This conclusion transfers
to the comparator class when the supplied graph excludes its additional
shared-exogenous structures, because the two compatible classes then
coincide.  Without class equality, constancy on a subclass supplies no
conclusion about the extra elements of a strict superclass.

For completeness, unsupportedness by itself does not force failure.  A
two-node acyclic target with a supported fair binary node \(A\), an
unsupported binary node \(X\) having success probability \(q\), independent
ground noises, and event \(B=\{A=X\}\) has
\[
 P(B\mid\operatorname{do}(a))
 =(1-q)\frac12+q\frac12=\frac12,
\]
although the row of \(X\) occurs directly in every event term.  Thus the
unsupported row can cancel from the query.  Type sharing is load bearing
for the asserted one-parameter class: with two independent target nodes
using the same unsupported binary key and the event of exactly one
success, the shared-row map is
\[
 2q(1-q)\leq\frac12.
\]
If type sharing is removed while all other features of this finite
acyclic example are retained, occurrence-specific probabilities
\(q_1=1\) and \(q_2=0\) make the event probability one.  This supplies the
required small-instance check and shows why the common coordinate \(q\)
cannot be replaced silently by occurrence-specific rows.
